page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance provides 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. System memory totals 48.0 GB, yielding a resource density of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression both falling into the bottom 25% tier. Conversely, multi-core capabilities are more robust, with stress-ng multi-core performance, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, and Geekbench multi-core scores all registering in the average middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth tests, including both cached small-block and uncached large-block reads and writes, also consistently perform within the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g6.3xlarge offers a balanced allocation of compute and memory resources, making it a viable option for workloads that can leverage parallel processing to overcome its single-core limitations. The lack of bundled local storage means storage-heavy applications will rely on external network-attached volumes. This instance is suited for multi-threaded workloads such as static web serving, Redis database operations, software compilation, and general-purpose application hosting.
